name: Khua
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: [p.2, sec.2.1] Phonological words in Bru Tri as in other Katuic languages are either mono- or disyllabic. Because a word with two syllables always has an unstressed first syllable and a dominant second syllable, these languages have sometimes been described as “sesqui-syllabic.” [...] [p.4, sec.2.4] Word stress is always found on the final (main) syllable. Yes-no questions are often accompanied by rising intonation and use of the clause-final question particle /tə:/. Other interrogatory sentences are marked by stress on the question marker.
new_statements.citation: Miller, Carolyn P. 2017. Eastern Bru Grammar Sketch [running head 'Bru Tri Grammar Sketch']. SIL Language and Culture Archives (REAP). 40 pp. (downloaded from the Internet Archive copy of the sil.org REAP file, 2023-12-08).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (unstressed pre-syllable + main syllable); word stress always falls on the final, main syllable. Corroborated for the Quang Tri (Huong Hoa) Van Kieu dialect by Phillips & Miller 1976:217 n.4 (pre-syllable non-stressed, main syllable stressed).
new_statements.exceptions: None for word stress. Pre-syllable vowel is normally a neutral mid-central vowel or syllabic nasal; only 'in a very few words' is the pre-syllable vowel contrastive (/kucit/ 'die' vs /kacit/ 'kill'). Sentence level: interrogatives other than yes-no questions carry stress on the question marker.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement about the phonological word (max. (CV(C))C(C)V(C)); intonation remarks concern clause-final particles. The sketch describes Eastern Bru (Bru Tri in Laos / Bru Van Kieu in Vietnam; author's own fieldwork dialect originally Huong Hoa, Quang Tri); it names Khua only as one of the groups subsumed under the Van Kieu exonym and contains no Khua-specific data.
new_statements.identity_note: khua1243 'Khua' [xhv] is a retired Glottolog bookkeeping entry: per Glottolog (citing Vargyas 2000) the Khua speak a dialect of Eastern Bru [bru] = east2332 (the ISO entry stems from Wurm & Hattori 1981:35, which also split off Mangkong and Tri). No description of Khua speech itself was found anywhere (OLAC lists nothing; Glottolog has zero Katuic 'Khua' titles). The quoted statement is Carolyn Miller's for Eastern Bru (Bru Tri / Bru Van Kieu; her fieldwork dialect Huong Hoa, Quang Tri), a sketch that names Khua only as one of the groups under the Van Kieu exonym. The statement and the saved files therefore belong under east2332 (a separate target in this reading whose earlier scan was the named source could not be reached - the Miller 2017 PDF with text layer and the two MKS scans saved here are directly usable for it). Under the code-currency rule a retired code should not be counted as a separate catalog language, hence not proposed for the catalog despite a first-hand quote being held by the project.

sources.note: p.2 sec.2.1: a disyllabic word 'always has an unstressed first syllable and a dominant second syllable' (sesquisyllabic); p.4 sec.2.4: 'Word stress is always found on the final (main) syllable.' p.1 states the Van Kieu exonym covers Tri, Khua and Mangcong; the variety described is Eastern Bru (Bru Tri / Van Kieu), not Khua speech specifically.
